direction.body:
User report (2026-10-12), comparing with Solo's notifications. The user's words: "we need elegant notifications like solo term we don't have notifications at all - I don't want the icon in the bar soloterm has nor the list I just want the clean notifications and sound and it stauys for a momnet as a toaster and auto hides".

Asked which events notify, the user picked: an Agent needs them, an Agent fails, and an Agent changes their Todo or Pad. They did not pick an Agent finishing. Asked what happens while roundup is not the app in front, they picked "sound only": the sound plays at once, and the toast shows when they come back.

## Seen, and why (on `main`)

| Seen | Cause |
|---|---|
| Nothing tells the user when an Agent needs them, fails or edits their work, unless they are looking at it | No toast and no sound exist in the App. The Dock badge (`rail/DockBadge.tsx`) only counts |

## Outcome

- A toast shows, with a short sound, when:
  - an Agent's Kind becomes `needs-you`;
  - an Agent's Kind becomes `error`;
  - an Agent changes a Todo the user created or a Pad the user owns.
- The toast is small and clean: the Agent's Glyph, its name and one line of what happened. It stays for a moment, then hides by itself. Hovering it keeps it.
- Clicking a toast opens what it names: the Agent, or the Todo's or Pad's Drawer.
- While roundup is not the app in front, the sound plays at once. The toast shows when the user comes back.
- No bell icon, no badge in the window bar and no list of past notifications.
- No toast for the Agent the user has selected while roundup is in front.

## Scope

- Webview: a toast layer in `apps/desktop/src`, driven by the events the App already receives.
- If playing the sound while roundup is in the background needs the App, that is a new App seam command and follows the Contract recipe (AGENTS.md rule 4).
- The toast's motion uses the `animate` skill. With reduced motion, toasts appear and leave without movement.

## Regression requirements

- A toast never covers the input the user types in, the traffic lights or the window's title.
- Many events at once show as few toasts, not a wall.
- AGENTS.md rule 7: no extra work while nothing notifies.
- AGENTS.md rule 8: name the Checks the change moves, use only Tokens, break no Check that passes on `main`.

Related: #1104.

direction.body:
## Outcome

Toasts look and move like AffectUI's Notification Stack and Toaster, and none stays on screen forever. Each Toast shows how long it has left as a thin bar that drains, the way Solo (soloterm.com) does. When the bar empties, the Toast hides.

## Owner's words

> Their toasters and notification and animations are really good https://www.affectui.com/components/notification-stack
> We also should never keep notifications for ever it should has a time and a progress bar like soloterm

## Scope

- Every Toast has a timer, including U80's one failure line, which today has none (`toasts/queue.tsx`). The spec sets the times; a failure may stay longer than a notice, but never without end.
- The bar drains with the remaining time. It pauses, and the timer with it, while the pointer or keyboard focus is in the stack and while the window is hidden. It resumes from where it was; U503's five-second restart after hover or focus becomes this pause-and-resume.
- Stack look: cards sit behind each other, the ones behind smaller and peeking out. Hover or focus fans the stack out into a list.
- Keep U410–U414 and U503: event exclusions, selected-Agent suppression, one chime, away holding without replayed sound, coalescing, at most three cards including the summary, Escape dismissal, target navigation.
- Notification Stack is free and MIT: its CSS may be copied with credit. Toaster is a paid Pro item: rebuild from its public docs (`https://www.affectui.com/llms-full.txt`, "Toaster"), copy no code. Tokens only; the existing Ark toast stays the base.

## Motion

- A new Toast lifts in from the edge; the cards behind move back. A dismissed or expired card fades and sinks a few pixels while the rest move up.
- The bar's drain is the only motion with no act behind it. It runs only while the Toast is visible and the window is shown (#3298).
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` cards switch at once and the bar still drains: it is the only way to see the time left.

## Regression

- Floating layer order holds (#3291, #3295); no layout shift under the stack (#3294).

direction.body:
## Outcome
The owner writes their own named actions in a config file; they appear in the Switcher and run with `rup do <name>` like built-in ones.

## Outside evidence
Outside evidence: the owner studied Rex, Superlogical's Mac terminal multiplexer, and its docs (https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/llms-full.txt). Rex's Lua config defines custom actions by name with arguments; they appear in the command palette, bind to keys, and run with `rex do <name>`; `rex actions` lists the loaded ones.

## Scope
First build `docs/extension-interface.md`'s `register(on)` (an Extension module, its manifest and its permissions, enforced by rupd); no host exists yet. Decide where Extensions run and name that module. Then specify two implementation Issues, in order: the `register` host, and the Switcher showing user actions in `apps/desktop`. Depends on the named action list (its specification blocks this one).

This is a specification run. Write the acceptance for the whole lesson in `scenarios/user-actions.md` as bounded given/when/then scenarios, each with a named observer. Then edit each Issue this one blocks so its `Scenarios:` line names its IDs, and close this Issue from the specification PR. Change no product code.

## Regression requirements
A throwing Hook is skipped with one Toast (fail open). Permissions are declared and enforced. A user action cannot take a built-in name.

Source: the owner accepted this Rex UX lesson (15) on 2026-10-31.
